title: Enhanced weak-field sensing using detuned squeezing
authors: Li-Wen Zhang, Yang Liu, Han-Jie Zhu, Wei Qin
abstract: Achieving measurement precision beyond the standard quantum limit (SQL) is a fundamental object in quantum metrology. In this manuscript, we propose a streamlined protocol for weak signal sensing in a trapped-ion spin-oscillator system that simultaneously exploits detuned motional squeezing and spin-oscillator entanglement. By combining these two quantum resources, the phase accumulation in this spin system is significantly accelerated, as a result achieving an exponential improvement in the sensitivity over unsqueezed cases. Remarkably, we show that the significant metrological gain provided by our protocol persists in noisy environments, with the sensitivity remaining below the SQL. In particular, our protocol retains a distinct advantage in the short interrogation time regime, thus demonstrating the practical potential in quantum-enhanced sensing.
summary: This paper proposes a novel quantum sensing protocol for trapped-ion spin-oscillator systems to measure weak fields with enhanced precision. By simultaneously utilizing detuned motional squeezing and spin-oscillator entanglement, the protocol achieves an exponential improvement in sensitivity over standard methods. The analysis confirms that this quantum advantage persists even in the presence of realistic technical noise.
main_problem: The primary goal is to achieve measurement precision for weak-field sensing that surpasses the Standard Quantum Limit (SQL).
main_result: The proposed protocol achieves an exponential improvement in sensitivity over unsqueezed cases by combining detuned motional squeezing and spin-oscillator entanglement.
method: The authors develop a streamlined, single-step protocol that maps the weak field signal onto the spin phase shift, quantifying sensitivity using the Quantum Fisher Information (QFI).
model_or_system: The system modeled is a trapped-ion spin-oscillator system. The dynamics are governed by a Hamiltonian involving detuned parametric amplification (DPA) coupling the spin ($\hat{\sigma}_z$) to the motional mode ($\hat{a}$).
key_observables: Quantum Fisher Information (QFI), Quantum Cramér-Rao Bound (QCRB), accumulated phase $\phi(T)$, and the final expectation value $\langle\hat{\sigma}_yangle_f$.
important_parameters: Detuning ($\Delta_c$), squeezing degree ($r$), interrogation time ($T$), and noise parameters ($\sigma, \Gamma, \kappa$).
main_assumptions: The analysis considers the system's evolution under the influence of various noise sources, including frequency fluctuations, spin decoherence, and motional damping.
figures_summary: Figure 2 illustrates Wigner functions and schematic spin states for the motional mode loop. Figure 3 shows the time evolution of the mean phonon number.
paper_structure: The paper introduces the problem of surpassing the SQL, details the Hamiltonian and the combined squeezing/entanglement protocol, derives the sensitivity using QFI, and analyzes the performance in both ideal and noisy environments.
why_interesting: This work is highly relevant as it directly tackles quantum metrology using trapped ions, a canonical platform in AMO physics. The combination of squeezing and entanglement to achieve super-SQL scaling is a key theoretical advance.
